title.es: Apple lanzará cuatro productos (PRODUCT)RED la próxima semana
title.en: Apple to Release Four (PRODUCT)RED Products Next Week

body.es: Apple planea lanzar versiones (PRODUCT)RED del HomePod mini 2 y AirPods Max 2 el 1 de diciembre, coincidiendo con el Día Mundial del Sida y el 20.º aniversario de la organización RED. Según Mark Gurman, también se incluirán una correa de muñeca para AirPods Pro y una banda deportiva para Apple Watch en este color. El regreso de la línea roja busca capitalizar la temporada de compras navideñas tras un periodo sin nuevas ediciones especiales.
body.en: Apple plans to release (PRODUCT)RED versions of the HomePod mini 2 and AirPods Max 2 on December 1st, coinciding with World AIDS Day and the 20th anniversary of the RED organization. According to Mark Gurman, a Wrist Strap for AirPods Pro and a Sport Band for the Apple Watch will also be included in this color. The return of the red line aims to capitalize on the holiday shopping season after a period without new special editions.

evidence.claim: Apple plans to release (PRODUCT)RED versions of the AirPods Max 2 and HomePod mini 2 on or around Tuesday, December 1.
Apple is planning to release an additional two accessories in the (PRODUCT)RED color: a Wrist Strap for AirPods Pro and a Sport Band for the Apple Watch.
The (PRODUCT)RED version of the HomePod mini 2 will have a red mesh exterior.
Apple has partnered with the (RED) brand to raise money for The Global Fund since 2006.
Apple had not offered the (PRODUCT)RED option for some products for a while now.

title.es: Tidal bloqueará la música generada por IA a partir del 9 de diciembre
title.en: Tidal to Block AI-Generated Music Starting December 9

body.es: Tidal ha anunciado que comenzará a bloquear la música generada por IA el 9 de diciembre, esperando rechazar entre 80.000 y 85.000 canciones al día. La plataforma justifica la medida señalando que el 96% de las canciones de IA no reciben ninguna reproducción. A diferencia de Apple Music, que introdujo etiquetas de transparencia para la IA, Tidal opta por una prohibición directa para proteger a los artistas y oyentes.
body.en: Tidal has announced it will start blocking AI-generated music on December 9, expecting to reject between 80,000 and 85,000 songs per day. The platform justifies the move by noting that 96% of AI songs receive zero plays. Unlike Apple Music, which introduced AI Transparency Tags, Tidal opts for a direct ban to protect artists and listeners.

evidence.claim: Tidal plans to start blocking AI music on December 9.
Tidal expects 80,000 to 85,000 songs to be rejected per day.
96 percent of AI songs get zero plays, according to Tidal.
Apple Music introduced AI Transparency Tags earlier this year.

title.es: Meta lanza su agente personal Muse en el Reino Unido
title.en: Meta Launches Its Personal AI Agent Muse in the UK

body.es: Meta ha desplegado su agente personal Muse en el Reino Unido, permitiendo a los usuarios completar tareas como enviar correos o reservar viajes. El agente puede utilizar credenciales de pago en el checkout a través de Link, una cartera segura para agentes desarrollada por Stripe. Muse está disponible solo para mayores de 18 años y se integra con marcas británicas como Marks & Spencer y ASOS.
body.en: Meta has rolled out its Muse personal agent in the UK, allowing users to complete tasks such as sending emails or booking travel. The agent can use payment credentials at checkout via Link, a secure wallet for agents built by Stripe. Muse is available only for those over 18 and integrates with British brands like Marks & Spencer and ASOS.

evidence.claim: Meta has rolled out its Muse personal AI agent to users in the United Kingdom.
Muse can complete tasks for users on their behalf, like sending an email or booking travel.
Muse can use payment credentials at checkout with Link, a secure wallet for agents built by Stripe.
Muse can only be used by people aged 18 and over.
Meta says Muse is launching in the U.K. with popular global Connectors, and it also partners with British brands and retailers.

title.es: Engadget: El iPhone 18e podría tener un módulo de cámara elevado
title.en: Engadget: iPhone 18e May Feature a Raised Camera Module

body.es: Según imágenes CAD vistas por Engadget, Apple está considerando un rediseño del módulo de cámara para el iPhone 18e. Los renders muestran un bump casi cuadrado de unos 28 mm por 35 mm que aloja la cámara trasera, el flash LED y el micrófono. Esto marcaría un cambio respecto al iPhone 17e actual, cuyo lente tiene una pequeña protuberancia pero se mantiene plano contra la parte trasera del teléfono.
body.en: According to CAD images seen by Engadget, Apple is considering a redesign of the camera module for the iPhone 18e. The renders show an almost square bump measuring about 28 mm by 35 mm that houses the rear camera, LED flash, and microphone. This would mark a change from the current iPhone 17e, whose lens has a small protrusion but sits flush against the back of the phone.

evidence.claim: The iPhone 18e is expected to have a redesigned camera module with a camera bump.
The current iPhone 17e does not have a camera bump, but the lens has a small protrusion and sits flush against the back of the phone.

title.es: PrismML lanza Bonsai 2.5 para IA en dispositivo
title.en: PrismML Releases Bonsai 2.5 for On-Device AI

body.es: PrismML ha publicado Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, una actualización del modelo introducido en septiembre. Esta versión mejora las capacidades de codificación y el uso de herramientas para modelos que se ejecutan localmente en el dispositivo. El enfoque en modelos ternarios busca optimizar el rendimiento y la eficiencia energética en hardware de consumo.
body.en: PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model introduced in September. This version improves coding capabilities and tool use for models running locally on-device. The focus on ternary models aims to optimize performance and energy efficiency on consumer hardware.

evidence.claim: PrismML has released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an update to the model it introduced in September.

title.es: Los agentes de IA generan un 450% más de tráfico de red
title.en: AI Agents Generate 450% More Network Traffic

body.es: Un análisis indica que las tareas realizadas por agentes de IA generan un 450% más de tráfico de red que las mismas tareas hechas por humanos. Esta demanda está impulsando el retorno de la inferencia a infraestructuras locales o cercanas, ya que el procesamiento en tiempo real es sensible a la latencia. Las empresas globales enfrentan nuevos desafíos para cumplir con las leyes de soberanía de datos que requieren el procesamiento dentro de fronteras nacionales.
body.en: An analysis indicates that tasks performed by AI agents generate 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by humans. This demand is driving inference back to on-premises or near-premises infrastructure, as real-time processing is sensitive to latency. Global enterprises face new challenges in complying with data sovereignty laws that require processing within national borders.

evidence.claim: AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers.
AI inference is pushing infrastructure back on premises.
Network modernization is an ongoing project that requires a holistic approach.
Large enterprises may need on-premises or near-premises inference, which reverses years of cloud-first consolidation.
Data sovereignty and sovereign AI will create infrastructure challenges for global enterprises.

title.es: Versine lanza MCP para enviar dinero con IA
title.en: Versine Launches MCP for Sending Money with AI

body.es: Versine, una startup de YC F26, ha lanzado una plataforma MCP que permite enviar y solicitar dinero hablando con asistentes de IA. Cada usuario tiene una wallet de stablecoins auto-custodiada que almacena USDC en Base. Los pagos requieren la aprobación del usuario mediante passkey, creando un permiso de un solo uso para la transacción.
body.en: Versine, a YC F26 startup, has launched an MCP platform that allows users to send and request money by talking to AI assistants. Each user has a self-custodial stablecoin wallet storing USDC on Base. Payments require user approval via passkey, creating a one-time permission for the transaction.

evidence.claim: Versine is an MCP that allows users to send and request money through AI assistants.
Each user has a self-custodial stablecoin wallet storing USDC on Base.
Users can send money to people without a Versine account, and the recipient can cash out to their bank in 2 minutes.
Versine requires user passkey approval for one-time payments.

title.es: AWS PrivateLink disponible en Vercel Secure Compute
title.en: AWS PrivateLink Available on Vercel Secure Compute

text.es: Los equipos empresariales pueden crear y gestionar endpoints de AWS PrivateLink directamente desde el dashboard de Vercel. Cada red Secure Compute incluye un endpoint, con adicionales a $30/mes y transferencia de datos a $0,04/GB.
text.en: Enterprise teams can create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard. Each Secure Compute network includes one endpoint, with additional ones costing $30/month and data transfer at $0.04/GB.

evidence.claim: Enterprise teams can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard.

text.en: Yann LeCun, a proponent of open-source AI development, has criticized Anthropic's hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models, highlighting the debate on gatekeeping in the industry.

developer_signals.author: zachlloydtweets
developer_signals.original_text:
Here are the problems that I see happening if you let AI assistants or other agent systems like factories assume your own identity when they act on your behalf, from least problematic to most.

1/ They send slop on your behalf that folks think is yours (ok, fine)
2/ They “accidentally” do dumb stuff you might not want (my Instinct responded to a password reset email that I didn’t request, not good).
3/ They are prompt-injected by a malicious actor (e.g. someone sends you a gmail telling your agent to send you a bunch of sensitive data from other tools in your google workspace. very bad, as this can be the basis of a much wider attack)
4/ Nothing happens for a while, but then there is a skynet type moment and a very smart AI all of a sudden has the ability to impersonate everyone, spread disinformation, etc (i’m not fully there on this one, but calling it out regardless)

For Software Factories, the solution at least in part is to sandbox agents and have them use service accounts rather than human identity.

For AI assistants, the issue is that a lot of the stuff making them useful doesn’t support any kind of bot identity. 

It feels irresponsible to roll them out so quickly with such obvious security issues.

text.es: Zach Lloyd analiza los riesgos de seguridad cuando los agentes de IA actúan con la identidad del usuario, recomendando el uso de cuentas de servicio y sandboxing para evitar inyecciones de prompts y acciones no deseadas.
text.en: Zach Lloyd analyzes the security risks when AI agents act with the user's identity, recommending the use of service accounts and sandboxing to prevent prompt injections and unwanted actions.

developer_signals.author: HamelHusain
developer_signals.original_text:
I’m glad that more people are scrutinizing popular AI benchmarks.  

Eugene did a deep dive into 12 benchmarks and writes about the surprising things he found like:

1. Erroneous graders 
2. Misconfigured harnesses 
3. Unrealistic specifications that don’t resemble how people use AI 
4. Problems with environments 

He also makes a good arguments about cost per task and metrics that have been Goodhart-nerfed 

Highly recommended reading!

text.es: Hamel Husain recomienda un análisis de Eugene Yan sobre 12 benchmarks de IA, destacando errores en los evaluadores, configuraciones incorrectas y métricas que no reflejan el uso real de los modelos.
text.en: Hamel Husain recommends Eugene Yan's analysis of 12 AI benchmarks, highlighting errors in graders, misconfigured harnesses, and metrics that do not reflect real-world model usage.

developer_signals.author: swyx
developer_signals.original_text:
notable that a lot of the recent anthropic (and ant-alum) talks have been very specific about how much there is still left to do for human engineers, and if you are feeling depressed/anxious you need only look here / point your efforts towards AGI-aligned problems*:

- assume multiagent systems 1000x, from spawning subagents to being llm grader to advisor/sidekick pattern to dreaming/memory formation to collaborating peer to peer on a board. what breaks?
- Infra: unbundle Kubernetes to new filesystems, sandboxing, stateful, fast workflow orchestration (see @temporalio) at crazy scale. it's actors on steroids.
- Agent Authorization: EVERYONE agrees that having Instinct/Claude etc saving your password is bad (aka taking action On-Behalf-Of you instead of you delegating to an agent's own identity). (see @KeycardAI @okta etc) Then: how do agents trust another agent? 
- Security (hardening/patching core software), and Isolation (assuming compromise, limit blast radius)
- Monitoring (write-only OTel tracing across agents, linked to kill switches that dont fire false positives confusing agent persistence for malice)

actually an incomplete list! you can work at the harness level (https://t.co/mfsPv7KVv4) or solve Fermat's last theorem (https://t.co/MQO3JlDqkj) but who's counting anymore

*all of which katelyn happens to be hiring for haha

text.es: swyx destaca las áreas donde los ingenieros humanos aún son cruciales en la era de los agentes: infraestructura, autorización de agentes, seguridad y monitoreo, citando charlas recientes de Anthropic.
text.en: swyx highlights areas where human engineers are still crucial in the agent era: infrastructure, agent authorization, security, and monitoring, citing recent talks from Anthropic.

developer_signals.author: petergyang
developer_signals.original_text:
I've been using Gemini 4 Neon and @antigravity all weekend and made a free video course on how you can get the most out of this combo.

Some takeaways:

1. Orchestrator and /swarm are very useful for planning and building with multiple agents. At one point, I had 42 agents running at once.

2. /grill-me is a great built-in skill that gets Antigravity to ask clarifying questions to help you flesh out the plan first.

3. Remote control is better than Claude Code's because every thread is active by default. I show you how to add Antigravity to your phone home screen to run this in the video.

📌 Watch my full 17-minute Antigravity course here: https://t.co/lmfSTiVBsm
